skill.name: backend-architect
skill.description: Design, review, and refactor backend systems using hexagonal architecture, DDD, SOLID principles, clean code, performance checks, and testing guidance.
skill.summary: Review backend designs and code with practical architecture, testing, and refactoring guidance.
skill.author: Bikach

security_audit.summary: All 115 static findings are false positives after contextual review. Weak-cryptography alerts matched the French word "des", while other alerts matched harmless identifiers and Markdown formatting. No malicious intent, prompt injection, cryptographic implementation, or automatic command execution was found.

content.value_statement: Backend design reviews often miss dependency problems, code smells, and testing gaps. This skill applies structured architecture guidance and prioritized checklists to propose clear improvements.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates code changes against hexagonal architecture and bounded context boundaries.
Reviews dependency direction using all five SOLID principles.
Detects documented code smells, including God Class, Feature Envy, and Primitive Obsession.
Suggests targeted refactorings with practical bad and improved examples.
Applies clean code, testing, and performance checklists.
Organizes findings by blocking, important, and improvement priorities.
limitations: Provides guidance from repository context but does not verify runtime behavior automatically.
Does not include dedicated security threat modeling or compliance frameworks.
Examples require adaptation to the project language, framework, and conventions.
Architecture recommendations depend on complete requirements and representative code context.

use_cases.title: Feature architecture for backend developers
use_cases.description: Define bounded contexts, ports, adapters, domain models, and dependency direction before implementation.

use_cases.title: Code review for technical leads
use_cases.description: Review changes for architectural violations, code smells, testing gaps, and performance risks with prioritized feedback.

use_cases.title: Legacy refactoring for maintainers
use_cases.description: Identify concentrated responsibilities and coupled dependencies, then plan incremental refactoring supported by tests.

prompt_templates.title: Basic clean code review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [file or module] for clean code issues. Identify the three most important problems and suggest focused improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a focused first review of a small code area.

prompt_templates.title: Feature architecture design
prompt_templates.prompt: Design [feature] for [system] using hexagonal architecture. Define the domain model, use cases, ports, adapters, and dependency direction.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this before implementing a new backend capability.

prompt_templates.title: Code smell refactoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [module] for documented code smells and SOLID violations. Propose an incremental refactoring plan with tests after each step.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this to improve a coupled or difficult module.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-context architecture review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [change set] across all affected bounded contexts. Trace dependencies, data flow, testing coverage, and performance risks. Prioritize findings from P0 to P2.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for advanced review of broad backend changes.

output_examples.input: Review the user registration service for dependency inversion.
output: P1 - The use case constructs a concrete repository, which couples domain logic to infrastructure.
Inject a repository port through the constructor and keep its interface in the domain layer.
Add a unit test with a repository double before changing the dependency.

output_examples.input: Design an order cancellation feature using DDD and hexagonal architecture.
output: Bounded context: Orders owns cancellation rules and order state transitions.
Use case: Cancel Order validates policy, updates the aggregate, persists through a repository port, and publishes through an event gateway.
Adapters: HTTP handles transport, persistence maps records, and messaging publishes the cancellation event.

output_examples.input: Review a product listing endpoint with slow database access.
output: P1 - The repository loads related records inside a loop, creating an N+1 query pattern.
Measure query count, add eager loading for required relations, and verify pagination.
Add an integration test for query behavior and compare latency before and after the change.

best_practices: Provide business requirements, affected files, and architectural constraints.
Request small, prioritized recommendations with explicit impact and validation steps.
Run tests and profiling after each refactoring or performance change.
anti_patterns: Do not request a full redesign without sharing the current boundaries and constraints.
Do not apply every pattern when a simpler design meets current requirements.
Do not refactor behavior without tests that protect the existing contract.

faq.question: What architecture styles does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on hexagonal architecture, Clean Architecture concepts, DDD, dependency injection, and SOLID principles.

faq.question: Can it review existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide files or a change set, and it can identify architecture issues, code smells, testing gaps, and performance concerns.

faq.question: Does it modify code automatically?
faq.answer: It can propose implementation and refactoring changes when repository tools are available. Review and test every change before adoption.

faq.question: Which code smells are included?
faq.answer: It covers God Class, Feature Envy, Primitive Obsession, Shotgun Surgery, Data Clumps, and Long Method.

faq.question: Does it perform security review?
faq.answer: No. Its references do not provide dedicated threat modeling, vulnerability scanning, or compliance checks.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect P0 to P2 findings with locations, impact, recommended solutions, and relevant examples.
